title: The Year Summer Never Came
script: In 1816, snow fell in June and crops failed across parts of Europe and North America. The cause was not bad luck. Mount Tambora had erupted the year before, throwing enormous amounts of material into the atmosphere. Global temperatures dropped, harvests collapsed, and the year became known as the Year Without a Summer.

title: The Flood Made of Molasses
hook: Boston was once hit by a deadly wave of molasses.
script: In 1919, a huge storage tank burst in Boston and released more than two million gallons of molasses. The wave rushed through nearby streets, damaging buildings and killing 21 people. Cold weather later thickened the molasses, making rescue work even harder. The event became known as the Great Molasses Flood.

title: The War That Lasted Less Than an Hour
hook: One war ended before most movies reach their opening credits.
script: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 is commonly described as the shortest recorded war. After an ultimatum expired, British ships fired on the palace in Zanzibar. The fighting lasted roughly 40 minutes before the palace flag was lowered and resistance ended.

title: Sharks Are Older Than Trees
hook: Sharks existed before the first trees appeared.
script: The earliest shark-like fish appeared more than 400 million years ago. Trees arrived later, with the first forests developing roughly 385 million years ago. That means shark ancestors were already swimming in ancient oceans before Earth had anything resembling a modern forest.

title: The Animal With Cube-Shaped Droppings
hook: One animal produces cubes, and scientists know how.
script: Wombats are famous for producing cube-shaped droppings. Researchers found that different sections of the wombat intestine stretch at different rates. As the material dries and moves through the gut, those uneven contractions form distinct corners and flat sides.

title: The Eiffel Tower Changes Height
hook: The Eiffel Tower is taller in hot weather.
script: Metal expands when it warms. Because the Eiffel Tower is made largely of iron, summer heat can make the structure grow by several centimeters. When temperatures fall, the metal contracts again. The tower is quietly changing height throughout the year.

title: Octopuses Have Three Hearts
hook: An octopus has three hearts, but one stops working when it swims.
script: Two octopus hearts pump blood through the gills. A third circulates blood through the rest of the body. When an octopus swims, that main heart temporarily stops beating, which helps explain why octopuses often prefer crawling to sustained swimming.

title: The Ancient Computer Found Underwater
hook: Divers found a two-thousand-year-old machine inside a shipwreck.
script: The Antikythera mechanism was recovered from an ancient Greek shipwreck. Its interlocking bronze gears could track astronomical cycles and predict events such as eclipses. Built more than two thousand years ago, it is often described as the oldest known analogue computer.

title: The Town That Has Been Burning for Decades
hook: A fire has been burning underneath one American town for decades.
script: A coal-seam fire began beneath Centralia, Pennsylvania, in 1962. It spread through abandoned mine tunnels and proved extremely difficult to extinguish. Dangerous gases and unstable ground eventually forced most residents to leave, while the underground fire continued burning.

title: The Lake That Coats Animals in Minerals
hook: This lake can coat dead animals in a stone-like crust.
script: Lake Natron in Tanzania is extremely alkaline because of minerals carried in from the surrounding volcanic landscape. Animals that die in the water can become coated and preserved by mineral salts. They are not instantly turned to stone, but the eerie mineralized remains inspired that popular description.
